Geographic focus:
United States

Temporal focus:
T1. Historical report [NO]
T2. Forward-looking reporting short-term risks (next few weeks/months) [YES]
T3. Forward-looking reporting long-term risks (next quarters/years) [NO]

Synopsis:
US index futures are mildly higher ahead of the August NFP report. Fed Governor Waller tempered rate-hike expectations by signaling support for holding rates steady if inflation continues to ease, which pushed the implied probability of a hike down from 63% to ~50%. NFP is expected to rebound to +56K after July's surprise -23K print. Single-stock drag from LULU (-17.67%) and ADBE (-3.18%) is notable. Seasonal headwinds (September historically the weakest month) and upcoming CPI/PPI prints next week are additional near-term risk factors.

Q01. Is the content's main message on the US economy, US yields, US interest rates?
Relevance: YES

Q02. Is the content about increasing US interest rates?
Relevance: 45 (Moderate — a rate hike remains on the table and is the baseline risk being discussed, but Waller's comments shifted the narrative away from it)
Probability of increase: 50%

Q03. Is the content about holding stable US interest rates?
Relevance: 65 (Waller explicitly endorsed holding rates steady if inflation data cooperates, making this the dominant near-term base case)
Probability of holding: 50%

Q04. Is the content about decreasing US interest rates?
Relevance: 5 (Rate cuts are not discussed; the debate is squarely between hiking and holding)
Probability of decrease: ~0%

Q05. Focus on the very latest information: What is the sentiment/tone including the very latest information on US interest rates?
Sentiment: -35 (Moderately dovish shift — Waller's comments meaningfully pulled back hike expectations from 63% to ~50%, and his signal to hold if inflation abates is the last Fedspeak before the blackout, leaving markets in a less hawkish posture heading into the September meeting)
